q: How is CO2 counted for DRI made with syngas from coal gasification, as at Angul?
title: Coal gasification DRI: counting CO2
short: By carbon mass balance across the gasifiers and the DRI shaft: carbon in the coal fed in, minus carbon leaving in DRI, char, tar or sold by-products, times 44/12. CO2 stripped from the syngas and vented still counts. It can be subtracted only if sent to permanent geological storage.
audience: Gas based and syngas based DRI plants in Odisha and their steel buyers

ul: Into syngas, which reduces the ore and is partly burnt for heating.
Into CO2 removed by the acid gas removal unit, usually vented.
Into DRI as carbon content, and into ash, char and tar.

p: The DRI's direct emissions are all CO2 released from the gasification and reduction steps within the installation. The vented CO2 stream is often a large single source and must be metered or balanced.

Gasification and shaft reduction can use coal more efficiently than a rotary kiln, but the figure depends on the coal, the carbon left in the DRI and what happens to the CO2 stream. Work it out from your own data rather than assuming it is lower.
